title: Fake News on Social Media
text:
Many people read news on social media every day. Some news is true, but some news is fake. Fake news is a story that is not true, but it looks real. People share it fast because it is exciting.

Before you share a story, check where it comes from. Ask yourself if other websites report the same thing. If you are not sure, do not share it. This helps to stop fake news.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what is fake news?
options: A story that is not true but looks real
A video of a famous singer

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what should you ask yourself before you share a story?
options: If other websites report the same thing
How many people like the story
What time the story was written
Whether the story is very long

questions.text: Why might people share fake news without checking it?
options: They want to share exciting stories quickly

questions.text: What is the writer's main advice?
options: Check a story before you share it
Share every story with your friends

vocabulary.definition: to send something to other people
to look at something to see if it is correct

paragraph_translations: Birçok insan her gün sosyal medyada haber okur. Bazı haberler doğrudur, ama bazıları sahtedir. Sahte haber, doğru olmayan ama gerçek gibi görünen bir hikâyedir. İnsanlar bunu hızlıca paylaşır, çünkü heyecan vericidir.
Bir hikâyeyi paylaşmadan önce nereden geldiğini kontrol et. Kendine, diğer web siteleri aynı şeyi haber yapmış mı diye sor. Emin değilsen onu paylaşma. Bu, sahte haberleri durdurmaya yardımcı olur.
